description: Composite eight-panel figure mixing two plot types (group is genuinely composite). (a), (c), (e) and (g) are nanoindentation load–depth curves: x-axis "Depth (nm)" 0–350, y-axis printed as "Load (µm)" (0–14000, all curves plateau at ≈10000). (b), (d), (f) and (h) are hardness scatter charts, Hardness (GPa) versus Annealing Temperature (°C) (axis 400 or 800–1300), with error bars. (a) α-phase curves in the Ni-containing sample, legend: Solution-treated, 900 °C (α+B2), 900 °C (α), 1050 °C (α+B2), 1050 °C (α); (b) corresponding hardness values plus a secondary "Ni content in B2 (wt.%)" axis with a horizontal dashed line near its top. (c) austenite curves in the Ni-containing sample (nine conditions, 500 °C (γ+κ) through 1050 °C (γ)); (d) hardness plus a secondary "Mn content in κ-carbide (wt.%)" axis. (e) and (f) are α in the Ni-free sample, with printed labels 18.4 wt.% Mn, 24.8 wt.% Mn, 22.8 wt.% Al, 24.6 wt.% Al on the composite points. (g) and (h) are γ in the Ni-free sample, with printed 20.4 wt.% Mn, 25.3 wt.% Mn, 18.3 wt.% Al, 19.1 wt.% Al. Together the panels argue that precipitate-bearing composites (α+B2, γ+B2, α+κ, γ+κ) are markedly harder (roughly 6–10 GPa) than the parent α and γ phases (roughly 3–4 GPa) at all annealing temperatures in both alloys.
measured_quantities: indentation load (axis printed as 'Load (µm)', unit likely mis-rendered µN)

observations.observation: Panel (a) legend lists five indentation conditions for the Ni-containing α phase: Solution-treated, 900 °C (α+B2), 900 °C (α), 1050 °C (α+B2) and 1050 °C (α).

Every load–depth curve in (a), (c), (e) and (g) reaches a flat plateau at approximately 10000 on the load axis, while the load axis itself extends to 14000, i.e. the curves are plotted at a constant maximum load.

The load axis of the load–depth panels is printed as 'Load (µm)', a unit that is physically implausible for nanoindentation and is most likely a rendering of µN; the printed label is not a hardness or depth quantity.
In panel (b) the two α+B2 hardness points (900 °C and 1050 °C, Ni-containing sample) fall between the 9 and 10 GPa gridlines, while the α-only points cluster near the 3 GPa gridline.
Panel (b) carries a secondary right-hand axis labelled 'Ni content in B2 (wt.%)' with a horizontal dashed line running near the top of that axis across the whole plotted temperature range.

Panel (d) carries a secondary right-hand axis labelled 'Mn content in κ-carbide (wt.%)' with a horizontal dashed line near the upper end of that axis; the γ+κ hardness points sit near the 7 GPa gridline, γ+B2 near 8 GPa and γ near 3.5–4 GPa.
Panel (f) prints the compositions '18.4 wt.% Mn' and '24.8 wt.% Mn' beside the α+κ points and '22.8 wt.% Al' and '24.6 wt.% Al' beside the α+B2 points of the Ni-free sample.
Panel (h) prints the compositions '20.4 wt.% Mn' and '25.3 wt.% Mn' beside the γ+κ points and '18.3 wt.% Al' and '19.1 wt.% Al' beside the γ+B2 points of the Ni-free sample.

The caption assigns the four curve panels and four hardness panels as: (a)/(b) α and its composites in the Ni-containing sample, (c)/(d) austenite and its composites in the Ni-containing sample, (e)/(f) α and its composites in the Ni-free sample, (g)/(h) γ and its composites in the Ni-free sample.
The hardness values of the various phases in Figure 4 are stated to be summarised in Table 2.
The nanoindentation method used is stated to be unable to measure isolated nano-sized precipitates and instead gives a compound hardness of the matrix together with the particles.

The cited text reports two B2 morphologies: B2 with flat interfaces and sharp edges of average size ≈1.4 µm in the γ phase, and disk-like precipitates of a few hundred nanometres in the α phase; κ-carbide is cuboid (<100 nm) in γ and needle-like (average ≈1.5 µm) in α.
Nanoindentation was performed as a function of four annealing temperatures (500 °C, 700 °C, 900 °C and 1050 °C) and two alloy compositions, Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni and Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C (all in wt.%).

In both alloys the precipitate-bearing composite points (α+B2, α+κ, γ+B2, γ+κ) plot well above the parent-phase points on the hardness axes, i.e. the composites are harder than the single-phase α or γ regions.
Panel (h) contains the stray strings '700 °C (γ+κ)' and '1050 °C (γ)' in its upper-left corner, which do not match the (h) legend entries and appear to be residual text from panel (g).

subfigures.description: Load–depth curves for the α phase and its composites in the Ni-containing sample. Five legend entries: Solution-treated (light blue), 900 °C (α+B2), 900 °C (α), 1050 °C (α+B2), 1050 °C (α). Curves rise from 0 nm to a flat plateau at ≈10000 on the load axis between ≈200 and ≈310 nm depth; unloading branches are near-vertical.

Hardness (GPa) versus Annealing Temperature (°C) for the α phase and α+B2 composite of the Ni-containing sample; legend Solution-treated α, α+B2, α and Ni content. Two α+B2 points (900 and 1050 °C) lie between the 9 and 10 GPa gridlines; the α points cluster at ≈3 GPa. A secondary right-hand axis reads 'Ni content in B2 (wt.%)' with a horizontal dashed line near the top of that axis.

Load–depth curves for austenite (γ) and its composites in the Ni-containing sample; legend lists nine conditions: Solution-treated, 500 °C (γ+κ), 700 °C (γ+κ), 900 °C (γ), 500 °C (γ+κ+B2), 700 °C (γ+κ+B2), 900 °C (γ+B2), 1050 °C (γ+B2), 1050 °C (γ). Nine overlapping curves all plateau at ≈10000 load, the leftmost reaching it near 200 nm depth and the rightmost beyond 300 nm.

Hardness (GPa) versus Annealing Temperature (°C) for austenite and its composites in the Ni-containing sample; legend Solution-treated γ, γ+κ, γ+κ+B2, γ+B2, γ and Mn content. γ+κ points sit near 7 GPa (500 and 700 °C), γ+κ+B2 near 9 GPa (700 °C), γ+B2 near 8 GPa (900 and 1050 °C) and γ alone near 3.5–4 GPa. Secondary axis: 'Mn content in κ-carbide (wt.%)' with a horizontal dashed line near the top.

Load–depth curves for the α phase and its composites in the Ni-free sample; legend lists nine conditions: Solution-treated, 500 °C (α), 700 °C (α), 900 °C (α+B2), 1050 °C (α), 500 °C (α+κ), 700 °C (α+κ), 900 °C (α), 1050 °C (α+B2). Same axis ranges as (a); all curves plateau at ≈10000 load.

Hardness (GPa) versus Annealing Temperature (°C) for α and its composites in the Ni-free sample; legend Solution-treated α, α+κ, α+B2, α. Data points carry printed composition labels: '18.4 wt.% Mn' and '24.8 wt.% Mn' on the α+κ points (500 and 700 °C), '22.8 wt.% Al' and '24.6 wt.% Al' on the α+B2 points (900 and 1050 °C). α-only points lie near the 3 GPa gridline, composite points between 5 and 8 GPa.

Load–depth curves for austenite and its composites in the Ni-free sample; legend lists seven conditions: Solution-treated, 500 °C (γ+κ), 700 °C (γ+κ), 900 °C (γ), 900 °C (γ+B2), 1050 °C (γ), 1050 °C (γ+B2). Curves are tightly bunched and plateau at ≈10000 load between ≈270 and ≈320 nm depth.

Hardness (GPa) versus Annealing Temperature (°C) for γ and its composites in the Ni-free sample; legend Solution-treated γ, γ+κ, γ+B2, γ. Printed composition labels: '20.4 wt.% Mn' and '25.3 wt.% Mn' on the γ+κ points (500 and 700 °C), '18.3 wt.% Al' and '19.1 wt.% Al' on the γ+B2 points (900 and 1050 °C); γ-only points lie near 3.5–4 GPa. Stray text '700 °C (γ+κ)' and '1050 °C (γ)' appears at the upper left of the panel.
